title: From Reliance to Overreliance: Taxonomizing and Detecting Relational Risks in AI Companionship
abstract: arXiv:2611.25734v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Companion AIs are increasingly used for emotional support, yet distinguishing meaningful engagement from harmful reliance remains difficult. We introduce the Taxonomy of Relational Risks (TRR), which operationalizes users' emotional overreliance (EO) as observable conversational behaviors and separately identifies evidence of relational harm (RH), enabling empirical examination of when reliance behaviors co-occur with adverse consequences. Using naturalistic Character.AI and Replika conversations from 110 adults, we found EO-related behaviors in 63.2% of non-roleplay conversations, while observable relational harms appeared in 10.5%. Although EO did not necessarily lead to harm, recurring patterns often co-occurred with harmful outcomes, suggesting value as risk indicators. translated_title: 从依赖到过度依赖：AI陪伴中关系风险的分类与检测
translated_abstract: 伴侣型AI日益被用于情感支持，然而区分有意义的互动与有害的依赖仍然十分困难。我们提出了关系风险分类法，将用户的情感过度依赖操作化为可观察的对话行为，并单独识别关系伤害的证据，从而能够实证考察依赖行为何时与不良后果共同出现。通过分析110名成年人在Character.AI和Replika上的真实自然对话，我们发现63.2%的非角色扮演对话中存在与情感过度依赖相关的行为，而可观察到的关系伤害仅出现在10.5%的对话中。尽管情感过度依赖并不必然导致伤害，但反复出现的行为模式往往与有害结果共同出现，这表明其作为风险指标的价值。开源大语言模型在至少一种配置下能够令人满意地检测出14种情感过度依赖行为中的12种。定性分析揭示了对关怀的期待、反复的寻求支持……
tldr: 本文提出关系风险分类法，将AI陪伴中的情感过度依赖操作化为可观察的对话行为，基于110名用户的真实对话发现过度依赖行为普遍存在（63.2%）而实际关系伤害较少（10.5%），并验证了开源大语言模型可有效检测这些风险行为。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Taxonomy of Relational Risks (TRR), operationalizing emotional overreliance in AI companionship as observable conversational behaviors, finding such behaviors in 63.2% of natural user conversations while relational harms appeared in only 10.5%, and demonstrating that open-source LLMs can effectively detect these risk behaviors.
